## Overview

This is a markdown practice doc for some basic analysis in R working with data and event data. This is created in markdown for more effective commenting and highlighting questions for practice rather than usual R commenting. 


```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# load data
options(scipen=999) # turn off scientific numerical notation

`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`) # custom function for filtering data

# Specify packages
packages <-
  c("tidyverse","janitor","stringr","data.table",# general data wrangling
    "readxl","readr",
    "lubridate"
  ) 

# Install packages if not already installed
install.packages(setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages())))

# Load packages
sapply(packages, require, character.only = TRUE)

setwd(dirname(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path))

data <- read_csv("food_delivery_scooter_events.csv") 

glimpse(data)
# unique list of data to view
unique_vals <- lapply(data, unique)


```


### Question 1: How long does each delivery take, and which stores are fastest or slowest on average?


```{r echo=FALSE}

# "delivered" equals the time from the order being received to delivery being complete
# need to filter data, find diff time between time stamps and simple group/summarise

time_taken_df <- data %>%
  filter(event_type %in% c("order_received","delivery_complete")) %>%
  group_by(delivery_id) %>%
  arrange(delivery_id, event_timestamp) %>%
  mutate(time_taken = event_timestamp - lag(event_timestamp))

time_taken_deliv <- time_taken_df %>%
  select(delivery_id, time_taken) %>%
  filter(!is.na(time_taken))

time_taken_deliv_all <- time_taken_deliv %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarise(time_taken_avg = mean(time_taken)) %>% pull()

```
```{r}

time_taken %>%
  group_by(store_name) %>%
  summarise(time_taken_avg = mean(time_taken, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(time_taken_avg)

```

- Time taken on average for all deliveries is `r round(time_taken_deliv_all,2)`. 
- 
  
### Question 2: How long does each stage of the delivery journey take, and which stage is the biggest contributor to total delivery time?


```{r}
# calculate time diff between each event type
# then aggregate output to see event timings

time_taken_all_stages <- data %>%
  group_by(delivery_id) %>%
  arrange(delivery_id, event_id) %>%
  mutate(
    prev_timestamp = lag(event_timestamp),
    next_timestamp = lead(event_timestamp)
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    stage_time_taken = lead(event_timestamp) - event_timestamp,
    stage_time_taken2 = # diff method, formatted in mins
      as.numeric(difftime(next_timestamp, event_timestamp, units = "mins")
      )
    ) %>%
  ungroup()

time_taken_all_stages2 <- time_taken_all_stages %>%
  group_by(event_type) %>%
  summarise(
    stage_time_taken_all = sum(stage_time_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    stage_time_taken_avg = round(mean(stage_time_taken, na.rm = TRUE),2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(stage_time_taken_avg) %>%
  filter(!is.na(stage_time_taken_avg))

time_taken_all_stages2


```

- The longest stage for each delivery is the journey to the customer taking an estimated `r max(time_taken_all_stages2$stage_time_taken_avg` 


### Question 3: Which delivery events or stages are most associated with minor delays, and how long does the next stage take after a delayed event?

```{r}

# calculate how long delayed events take,
# compare how long delay vs normal operational
# check how deliveries with delayed compare to non delayed deliveries times - is this significant?
 
time_taken_all_stages <- data %>%
  group_by(delivery_id) %>%
  arrange(delivery_id, event_id) %>%
  mutate(
    prev_timestamp = lag(event_timestamp),
    next_timestamp = lead(event_timestamp)
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    stage_time_taken = lead(event_timestamp) - event_timestamp,
    stage_time_taken2 = # diff method, formatted in mins
      as.numeric(difftime(next_timestamp, event_timestamp, units = "mins")
      )
    ) %>%
  ungroup()

time_taken_delayed <- time_taken_all_stages %>%
  group_by(event_type, status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    stage_time_taken_avg = round(mean(stage_time_taken, na.rm = TRUE),2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(event_type, desc(status))

time_taken_delayed


```

Operationally per event, there isn't a meaingful distance across each event time stage timings where minor delays occur. 


```{r}

time_taken_all_stages %>%
  group_by(delivery_id) %>%
  mutate(
    delay_flag = if_else(any(status == "minor_delay"), TRUE, FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(delay_flag) %>%
  summarise(stage_time_taken_avg = round(mean(stage_time_taken, na.rm = TRUE),2))


```

Data on the surface is misleading and calculating this overall is misleading and skewed, as total distance is not taken into account which is one of if not the biggest factor at play in delivery times.
